strings.name: Gustavo Petro
strings.summary: Petro moved from the M-19 guerrilla movement into parliamentary politics, serving as senator and Bogotá mayor before becoming Colombia’s first left-wing president in 2022. He promoted peace, land and energy-transition agendas amid intense debate over reforms and security. The US sanctioned him in 2025; he disputed its allegations. His presidential term ended in 2026, succeeded by Abelardo de la Espriella.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; reviewed on 15 November. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Elected Colombia’s first left-wing president, advanced peace, land and energy-transition agendas and influenced regional politics.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Economics education at Universidad Externado de Colombia; further studies included public administration.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Political transition
strings.highlights.h1.text: Moved from guerrilla membership to parliament, city government and the presidency, altering Colombia’s established party landscape.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Reform agenda
strings.highlights.h2.text: Promoted peace, land and energy-transition proposals amid debate over implementation and security consequences.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Ended presidential term
strings.timeline.t1.text: His four-year term ended; Abelardo de la Espriella succeeded him.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Faced US sanctions
strings.timeline.t2.text: The US imposed drug-related sanctions; he disputed the allegations. Sanctions are not a criminal conviction.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Became president
strings.timeline.t3.text: Took office after election as Colombia’s first left-wing president.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Lost presidential runoff
strings.timeline.t4.text: Reached the presidential runoff and lost to Iván Duque.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became Bogotá mayor
strings.timeline.t5.text: Began serving as capital-city mayor, until 2015.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Entered Senate
strings.timeline.t6.text: Elected senator, drawing attention for exposing political links to paramilitary groups.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Entered lower house
strings.timeline.t7.text: Elected to the Chamber of Representatives after M-19’s demobilization.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Moved into legal politics
strings.timeline.t8.text: M-19 demobilized through a peace process; he had earlier been imprisoned for membership.
